claims.statement: The fixed radix is B=1000=2^3*5^3 and the canonical coefficient set is {0,...,999}.
claims.proof_reference: Part I; postulates K3-A1 and K3-A2

claims.statement: A finite coefficient profile a=(a_0,...,a_m), indexed from least significant to most significant, has value sum_i a_i*1000^i.
Every n in N_0 has exactly one finite canonical base-1000 coefficient profile.

scope.domain: n in N_0
assumptions: B=1000 is fixed
Every coefficient is the Euclidean remainder in 0..999
scope.boundary: Finite canonical expansions only; signed values are handled by the separate sign extension.

claims.statement: The symbol k is a lexical group separator; a terminal k denotes exactly one implicit low-order zero group.
Strict canonical words, K3-PAD imports and typed K3-RAW operands are distinct input types.
Euclidean carry/borrow normalization preserves the polynomial value and yields a canonical coefficient profile under the stated finite-vector assumptions.
claims.proof_reference: §§2.1–2.8, local balance and telescoping global invariant

scope.domain: Finite integer coefficient vectors
assumptions: Each local step uses Euclidean quotient and remainder
The input vector is finite
scope.boundary: The binary carry bound is not asserted for arbitrary signed raw coefficients.

claims.statement: For every r>=1, Z/1000^r Z is isomorphic to Z/2^(3r) Z x Z/5^(3r) Z.

scope.domain: r in integers with r>=1
assumptions: The moduli 2^(3r) and 5^(3r) are coprime
scope.boundary: This is a classical CRT specialization, not a claim that Z/1000^r Z is a field.

claims.statement: The inverse-limit completion for the 1000-adic ideal filtration is Z_2 x Z_5 as a topological ring.

scope.domain: Inverse system Z/1000^r Z for r>=1
assumptions: The transition maps are the canonical reduction maps
The inverse-limit topology is used
scope.boundary: The completion is a topological ring; it is not a field.

claims.statement: Canonicalization preserves numeric evaluation; structural equality and expression-tree equality remain separately typed.

scope.domain: The separately typed K3 canonical, PAD and RAW input profiles
assumptions: Canonicalization is defined only for accepted PAD/RAW inputs
The value map is the polynomial evaluation over B=1000
scope.boundary: Structural or AST equality is not implied by numerical equality.

claims.statement: The finite Hankel moment determinant admits the stated weighted squared-Vandermonde expansion for a finite nonnegative coefficient profile.

scope.domain: Finite nonnegative profiles a=(a_0,...,a_m) and finite moment order q
assumptions: Moment and Hankel matrices use the definitions in §3
scope.boundary: The determinant expansion is a Cauchy-Binet/Vandermonde specialization, not a general priority claim.

claims.statement: The position-and-length polynomial of maximal zero runs reconstructs the zero mask of the finite profile.

scope.domain: Finite profiles with zero positions in {0,...,m}
assumptions: The zero-run list contains all maximal zero intervals exactly once
scope.boundary: The zero mask does not recover nonzero coefficient magnitudes.

claims.statement: The finite lag spectrum satisfies the stated zero-lag, reciprocity and total-sum identities for aligned finite profiles.

scope.domain: Two finite aligned profiles with the same declared finite depth
assumptions: Out-of-range coordinates are handled according to the chapter's zero-extension convention
scope.boundary: The lag spectrum does not in general determine the complete pair of profiles.

claims.statement: For addition of two nonnegative canonical profiles, carry values are binary and the weighted local balance telescopes to the global sum identity.

scope.domain: Two finite nonnegative canonical K3 profiles
assumptions: Each input coefficient belongs to 0..999
The initial carry is zero
scope.boundary: Binary carry is not claimed for arbitrary raw signed coefficient vectors or an arbitrary number of addends.

claims.statement: The K3-M appendix contains five parameterized families of 937 records each, for 4685 unique identifiers; records instantiate five master schemes and are not 4685 independent discoveries.
claims.proof_reference: §§0, 3–5; five master schemas and catalogue tables
claims.verification_note: Awaiting validation on the 0.5.0 consolidated HEAD; no current-head CI verification is claimed.

claims.statement: The 1000-divisibility depth is the minimum of the quantized 2-adic and 5-adic depths.

scope.domain: n in Z\{0} and r in N_0
assumptions: v_2 and v_5 are the ordinary prime-adic valuations
scope.boundary: The base-1000 divisibility depth is a minimum of two quantized valuations, not an additive prime valuation.

claims.statement: The defect of additivity of 1000-divisibility depth under products is given by the exact two-channel compensation term stated in the chapter.

scope.domain: Nonzero integers x,y
assumptions: The two prime valuations are finite on nonzero integers
The complementarity term is defined from the remainders modulo 3
scope.boundary: Do not infer additivity of the 1000-divisibility depth.

claims.statement: The residue-tree branching coordinates at every level form the stated bijection between the 8-channel and 125-channel residue coordinates.

scope.domain: Finite level r>=1 of the residue tree
assumptions: The coordinate maps are those specified in §5
scope.boundary: The result is an explicit CRT coordinate description, not a new arithmetic base.

claims.statement: The 1000-adic ultrametric equals the maximum of the two channel ultrametrics under the chapter's definitions.

scope.domain: Distinct integers x,y with the channel metrics defined in §6
assumptions: Both channel metrics are defined from the 2- and 5-adic valuations
The product metric is their maximum
scope.boundary: No claim is made that either channel alone induces the K3 metric.

claims.statement: For independent uniform input groups and a fixed incoming carry, the conditional joint distribution of output group and next carry is the one stated in the chapter.

scope.domain: A,D independent and uniform on D_B; fixed c in {0,1}
assumptions: B is an integer >=2
R=(A+D+c) mod B
C'=floor((A+D+c)/B)
scope.boundary: The law is conditional on a fixed incoming carry and does not imply independence of R and C'.

claims.statement: Under independent uniform input groups and fixed incoming carry, Corr(R,C'|c)=-1/sqrt(3), for every integer base B>=2.

scope.domain: A,D independent and uniform on D_B; fixed c in {0,1}
assumptions: B is an integer >=2
R and C' are as defined in §7
The correlation is conditional on c
scope.boundary: The coefficient -1/sqrt(3) is not asserted for nonuniform or dependent inputs.

claims.statement: The associated graded ring of the 1000-adic ideal filtration on Z is isomorphic to (Z/1000Z)[T].

scope.domain: The ring Z with ideal filtration I^r=(1000^r)
assumptions: The associated graded ring uses I^r/I^(r+1)
The grading is by r>=0
scope.boundary: The graded ring is a classical construction for this filtration, not a field.

claims.statement: For bounded linear operators on a common space, swapping adjacent factors in a product changes the product by the surrounding factors times the commutator.

scope.domain: Finite products of bounded linear operators on one common normed space
assumptions: All factors are bounded and composable
The commutator is [A,B]=AB-BA
scope.boundary: The formula does not apply to nonlinear operators without a separate definition and proof.

claims.statement: Under the explicitly stated nearest-frame rounding model, cumulative duration error is bounded by the sum of the half-target-frame periods.

scope.domain: A finite sequence of nearest-frame resampling stages with positive target rates f_j
assumptions: Each stage contributes at most half a target frame of rounding error
Durations are compared in the same unit
scope.boundary: The theorem does not prove spectral equivalence, absence of aliasing or amplitude preservation.

claims.statement: A transition that only removes capabilities or budget cannot increase the represented feasible-state set under the stated subset order.

scope.domain: A transition system ordered by inclusion of feasible-state sets
assumptions: Each transition only removes capabilities or budget
The feasibility predicate is monotone with respect to the stated order
scope.boundary: This abstract result does not prove that a particular software system enforces its declared constraints.

claims.statement: A distributional law for the two-channel complementarity index may hold under an explicitly chosen random model.
A spectral classification of operator chains may be available for selected operator classes.
A dimensionally complete K3-X typing discipline may be developed for a larger class of homogeneous quantities.
Sharper cumulative error bounds may be proved for selected multistage resampling models.
A joint proof-evidence graph may be specified with machine-checkable provenance rules.
The Pytyliki-to-K3 document is an application-level mathematical reconstruction with explicit implementation and evidence boundaries, not a theorem about full runtime correctness.
The OPlague-to-K3 materials define an application mathematical model and provenance boundaries; they do not extend the base K3 axioms.
claims.proof_reference: Part XI and Part XII; K3 mapping and proof obligations

claims.statement: In Z/1000^r Z for every r>=1, a residue class is a unit exactly when it is coprime to 1000; the number of units is (2/5)*1000^r.
claims.proof_reference: Sections 4-5; Euler totient and the unit criterion for a finite quotient ring.

scope.domain: The finite quotient ring Z/1000^r Z for integer r>=1.
assumptions: r is a positive integer.
Residue classes are taken modulo 1000^r.
scope.boundary: This is a result about finite quotient rings; it does not assert that Z/1000Z is a field.

claims.statement: The number of nonzero zero divisors in Z/1000^r Z is (3/5)*1000^r-1 for every r>=1.
claims.proof_reference: Sections 4-5; complement of the unit group in the finite commutative ring.

scope.domain: The finite quotient ring Z/1000^r Z for integer r>=1.
assumptions: r is a positive integer.
The ring is commutative and finite.
scope.boundary: The count excludes the zero class and is not a statement about infinite completion zero divisors.

claims.statement: Every element of the 1000-adic completion has a unique infinite positional coefficient sequence with coefficients in {0,...,999}.
claims.proof_reference: Sections 4-7; coherent inverse-limit residues and uniqueness of the coefficient expansion.

scope.domain: The inverse-limit completion of Z under the ideals (1000^r).
assumptions: The element is represented by a compatible family of residues modulo 1000^r.
Each coefficient belongs to 0..999.
scope.boundary: This is a topological completion result and does not add infinite strings to the finite canonical parser.

claims.statement: The 1000-adic expansions of ordinary integers have finite support for nonnegative integers and an eventually-999 tail for negative integers.
claims.proof_reference: Sections 8-9; integer embedding and the positional tail classification.

scope.domain: The canonical embedding of Z into the 1000-adic completion.
assumptions: The coefficient expansion is the unique inverse-limit expansion.
The integer is viewed under the canonical ring embedding.
scope.boundary: The statement classifies expansions of ordinary integers, not all elements of the completion.

claims.statement: K3-M treats a finite coefficient profile as a typed object admitting distinct moment, convolution, positional, transport, entropy, spectral and carry-based descriptors.
claims.proof_reference: Part XXI; ten-layer morphology definitions and domain restrictions.

claims.statement: When adding q finite canonical nonnegative K3 profiles, each normalized positional carry is bounded by 0<=c_i<=q-1.
claims.proof_reference: Section 88; induction on the positional carry recurrence.

scope.domain: Finite positional addition of q canonical nonnegative coefficient profiles.
assumptions: q is a positive integer.
Every input coefficient lies in 0..999.
Carry normalization follows the stated low-to-high recurrence.
scope.boundary: The bound concerns ordinary nonnegative canonical profiles; it does not cover arbitrary signed raw coefficients without a separate Euclidean balance model.

claims.statement: Directed K3 block composition is ordered concatenation of compatible finite positional block sequences and is distinct from integer addition and numeric evaluation.
claims.proof_reference: Part XXII; the definition and typed domain of ◇K3.

claims.statement: The DAK materials define typed mathematical models for operating-system states, resources, IPC, authority, graphs, networks, UI, audio and transactions without claiming implementation in Kaskad.
claims.proof_reference: Part XXIII, sections 94 and 97; DAK system model and cross-domain encoding contract.

claims.statement: The Reaper materials define typed mathematical models for compiler IR, bytecode, source spans, memory regions, module graphs and ABI boundaries without claiming runtime implementation in Kaskad.
claims.proof_reference: Part XXIII, sections 95 and 97; Reaper model and cross-domain encoding contract.

claims.statement: The VentuSample materials define typed discrete-signal and DSP mathematical models with explicit units and provenance, without claiming physical or runtime implementation in Kaskad.
claims.proof_reference: Part XXIII, section 96; discrete-signal and audio-domain model.
